digest.top_line: PEACE-1 at 7.7 y: abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (0.65-0.87) in de novo mCSPC; triplet vs ADT+docetaxel mOS 6.2 vs 4.4 y (HR 0.68).
digest.tldr: Prostate carries the day: PEACE-1 matures abiraterone's OS benefit in de novo mCSPC (HR 0.75), with SOC+RT mOS 4.6 y matching SOC and no RT-attributable HR reported. Breast brings two single-arm HER2+ CNS phase IIs pairing local RT with HER2 agents: BRIDGET (tucatinib after SRS, iPFS not reached) and INSPIRE-LM (RT then IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab, mOS 36.2 mo).

sites.intro: Two single-arm phase IIs in HER2+ CNS disease pair RT (SRS; WBRT or proton CSI) with HER2-directed therapy, and neither has a randomized control.

studies.name: BRIDGET
studies.tldr: Median iPFS not reached at 19.6 mo f/u (p<0.0001 vs historical 5.0 mo) adding tucatinib to HP/T-DM1 after SRS for isolated intracranial progression.
details: 🔍 Single-arm phase II, 48 enrolled, 47 evaluable; HER2+ MBC with 1st or 2nd isolated intracranial event
🔍 Stable or no extracranial disease on HP or T-DM1; enrolled within 12 wks of SRS
🩻 SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm required; whole-brain RT exclusionary
💊 Tucatinib 300 mg BID added continuously to ongoing HP or T-DM1; no prior HER2/EGFR TKI
📊 Intracranial progression in 17 pts (36.2%); median iPFS not reached
📐 One-sample log-rank p<0.0001 vs H0 median iPFS 5 mo (one-sided α=0.05, 90% power)
📊 Extracranial progression rare: 2 pts (4.3%)
⚠️ Historical exponential control, not a randomized SRS + continued-backbone arm
⚠️ Enriched for favorable pts: 66% no ECD, 80.9% after first intracranial event, 93.6% on HP
⚠️ RANO-BM after SRS: post-SRS imaging change vs true progression not addressed in source
🔗 Rationale from HER2CLIMB intracranial activity (tucatinib + capecitabine/trastuzumab); BRIDGET tests it without capecitabine

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase II against a historical 5.0 mo exponential control; primary endpoint met but no randomized SRS plus unchanged-backbone comparator.
verdict.audience: HER2+ MBC, isolated intracranial progression post-SRS, stable/no ECD on HP or T-DM1

studies.significance: The RT read is what follows SRS: with all lesions ≥5mm treated and WBRT excluded, 18-mo iPFS was 59% once tucatinib joined the backbone, so systemic change may extend the SRS-only strategy. Local vs distant brain failure after SRS is not reported in source, which limits the read on salvage RT burden.
studies.monday_clinic: In HER2+ MBC with a first or second isolated brain progression treated with SRS while extracranial disease is stable on HP or T-DM1, this supports considering adding a CNS-active TKI over the guideline default of continuing the same regimen; it does not address pts needing WBRT or prior TKI exposure.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Single-arm phase II**, 48 enrolled, 47 evaluable. Median follow-up **19.6 mos** (95% CI 15.6–26.1).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: HER2+ MBC with a **first or second isolated intracranial event** and **stable or no extracranial disease** on HP or T-DM1; ECOG PS 0–2; no prior HER2/EGFR TKI. Median age 53.5 yrs, 66% ER+, 66% no ECD, 80.9% after first event.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Tucatinib 300 mg BID** added continuously to ongoing HP (93.6%) or T-DM1.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm**, enrollment within 12 wks of SRS. **Whole-brain RT exclusionary.** Dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** iPFS per RANO-BM vs a historical exponential control (median 5.0 mos), one-sample log-rank test, one-sided α=0.05, 90% power, N=43 evaluable.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary endpoint met: median iPFS **not reached**, p<0.0001. Extracranial progression in 2 pts (4.3%).

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G≥3 AEs in **15% (7/47)**; described as favorable. RT-attributable toxicity not separated in source.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: HER2CLIMB established tucatinib's intracranial activity with capecitabine/trastuzumab in a broader brain-met population. BRIDGET moves the agent earlier, after SRS for isolated CNS progression, and drops capecitabine.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HER2+ MBC with isolated, SRS-treatable intracranial progression, controlled extracranial disease and no prior TKI. Does not represent pts needing WBRT, progressing extracranially, or already TKI-exposed.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Cohort enriched for low-burden disease (66% no ECD, mostly first event). Pattern of intracranial failure (SRS-treated vs new lesions) not reported, and RANO-BM after SRS can misread treatment effect as progression.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Supports **early tucatinib after local therapy** over continuing the same regimen, the current guideline default. Whether the gain holds against an SRS-plus-unchanged-backbone control, and whether it reduces salvage brain RT, is unsettled.

studies.interpretation:
The question BRIDGET asks is a real gap in practice. Isolated brain progression on HP or T-DM1, with the body still controlled, is common in HER2+ MBC, and the standard approach is to treat the brain locally and keep the systemic regimen going. That approach assumes local therapy is enough and that the large-antibody backbone does little in the CNS. BRIDGET tests the alternative: leave the extracranial regimen alone, but add a brain-penetrant TKI right after SRS. The rationale comes from HER2CLIMB, where tucatinib showed intracranial activity with capecitabine and trastuzumab. BRIDGET moves the drug earlier and leaves out capecitabine, so it is a different question from HER2CLIMB, not a confirmation of it.

The result looks large against the benchmark. Median iPFS was not reached, compared with a historical median of 5.0 months, and 59% of pts were free of intracranial progression at 18 months. The weak point is the benchmark itself. A one-sample log-rank test against an assumed exponential median measures the cohort against a single number from older data. Nothing in the source shows that the historical population matches these pts: low-burden disease, mostly a first intracranial event, two-thirds with no extracranial disease, and all lesions covered by SRS. That is the group where SRS alone would also be expected to control the brain longest. So part of the gap over 5.0 months could come from selection and modern SRS, not from tucatinib. The p-value tells us the cohort beat the historical assumption. It does not tell us how much tucatinib added.

For a radiation oncologist, the missing piece is the pattern of failure. Of 17 intracranial progressions, the source does not say how many were in SRS-treated lesions and how many were new. A CNS-active drug would mainly be expected to cut distant brain failure, which is what drives repeat SRS and eventually WBRT. Without that split we cannot tell whether tucatinib is working where it should. RANO-BM assessment after SRS also has a known confounder: imaging changes from treatment effect can look like progression, and the source does not describe how this was handled. That could push the iPFS estimate in either direction.

The low extracranial progression rate (4.3%) and G≥3 AEs of 15% suggest the strategy is tolerable and does not cost body control. But extracranial disease was stable or absent at entry by design, so this mostly reflects who was enrolled.

What would make the signal wrong: a randomized comparison where SRS plus an unchanged backbone matches these intracranial control rates in a similarly selected group. Until that trial exists, BRIDGET is a reasonable basis for adding a TKI case by case, especially in pts at high risk of distant brain failure. It is not yet grounds for making the TKI routine, and it says nothing about pts already exposed to a TKI or those whose disease requires WBRT.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SRS to all lesions ≥5mm with WBRT excluded, followed by tucatinib, gave 59% 18-mo iPFS, so systemic change may extend an SRS-only approach. The split between local failure and distant brain failure is not reported, so any effect on salvage SRS or WBRT burden is unknown.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Challenges the guideline default of continuing the same regimen after local therapy: adding tucatinib 300 mg BID to HP or T-DM1 gave 64% 12-mo and 59% 18-mo iPFS with G≥3 AEs 15%. Applies only to TKI-naive pts with stable or no extracranial disease.

open_questions: Benefit vs randomized SRS plus unchanged HP/T-DM1 backbone
Local vs distant intracranial failure pattern after SRS plus tucatinib
Activity with T-DM1 backbone given 93.6% received HP

studies.name: INSPIRE-LM
studies.tldr: mOS 36.2 mo (95% CI 19.4-NR), 12-mo OS 79% with RT then IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab in HER2+ breast LM; met predetermined OS endpoint.

details.text: 📊 Survival outcomes, single arm (N=30), median f/u 26 mo

details: 🔍 Multi-institutional single-arm phase II, N=30, enrolled Nov 2022 to May 2026
🔍 Eligibility: HER2+ breast LM, life expectancy > 8 wk, KPS ≥ 60
🔍 Baseline KPS ≤ 70 in 15 pts (50%); median age 48 (range 33-65)
💊 IT trastuzumab 80 mg + IT pertuzumab 80 mg (RP2D from phase I)
💊 Systemic agents could continue if controlling extra-CNS disease
🔍 RT: WBRT or proton CSI in 29 pts (97%), before IT or before study entry
⚠️ RT dose, fractionation, and WBRT vs pCSI split not reported in source

details.text: 📊 G≥2 AEs attributed to IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab

details: 📊 12 pts (40%) still on study therapy; longest treatment duration 38.7 mo
⚠️ RT waived after prior intracranial RT: RT contribution not separable from IT therapy
⚠️ Continued systemic HER2 therapy confounds attribution of OS to the IT regimen
⚠️ Prior systemic lines reported as median 34 (range 1-9): internally inconsistent, likely a typo

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase II, N=30, preliminary report with no randomised comparator; pre-study RT and continued systemic therapy confound what the IT regimen adds.
verdict.audience: HER2+ breast leptomeningeal metastasis, KPS ≥ 60, life expectancy > 8 wk

studies.significance: The regimen tested is RT then IT HER2 blockade, not IT alone: 29 pts (97%) had WBRT or proton CSI, some before study entry, and RT was waived after prior intracranial RT. Dose, fractionation and the WBRT vs pCSI split are unreported, so the result cannot yet tell you which RT field to pair with IT therapy.
studies.monday_clinic: In HER2+ breast LM with KPS ≥ 60 and life expectancy beyond 8 weeks, after WBRT or proton CSI, this supports IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab as a trial-backed consolidation option; it does not extend to HER2-negative LM or poor-performance pts.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multi-institutional **single-arm phase II**, N=30, enrolled Nov 2022 to May 2026. Median follow-up **26 mo**; preliminary report.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **HER2+ breast LM** with life expectancy > 8 wk and **KPS ≥ 60**. Median age 48; 15 pts (50%) had baseline KPS ≤ 70.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **IT trastuzumab 80 mg + IT pertuzumab 80 mg** after RT. Systemic agents could continue if controlling disease that LM developed on.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RT completed before IT therapy, but **not required** after prior intracranial RT. **WBRT or proton CSI** in 29 pts (97%), either before IT or before study entry; dose and fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** OS following study treatment. Secondary: LM-PFS and LM response.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Met its **predetermined OS endpoint**; survival and response numbers are in the detail table and response list.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G≥2 IT-attributed AEs were nausea/vomiting (10%), fatigue (7%) and headache (7%). No higher-grade toxicity breakdown in source.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Authors call this the longest median OS reported to date in HER2+ LM. The randomised MSKCC phase II of proton CSI vs photon involved-field RT is the leading RT reference for solid-tumor LM, but it did not test IT HER2 therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HER2+ breast LM pts with KPS ≥ 60 and life expectancy > 8 wk, mostly after WBRT or proton CSI. Does not represent HER2-negative LM, KPS below 60, or pts unable to receive IT therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: **RT and continued systemic therapy are uncontrolled co-interventions**, so OS reflects the whole package rather than IT therapy. LM response criteria are not specified, and the prior-lines figure in the abstract is internally inconsistent.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Durable OS with a low G≥2 AE burden supports IT HER2 blockade as a feasible consolidation after neuraxis RT in a selected HER2+ LM cohort. Whether it adds survival beyond modern CNS-active systemic HER2 therapy remains untested.

studies.interpretation:
The headline survival is striking for a disease where survival has historically been measured in months, but the trial was built to answer a feasibility and signal question, and it should be read that way. The cohort was selected on performance status and expected survival, it had a median age of 48, and it allowed systemic agents to continue when they were already controlling extracranial disease. Each of those choices enriches for pts with biology and fitness that predict longer survival regardless of the intrathecal regimen. In a less selected HER2+ LM population, including those with KPS below 60 or uncontrolled systemic disease, the effect would almost certainly look smaller.

For a radiation oncologist, the structure of the intervention matters more than the median. Nearly the whole cohort had whole-brain RT or proton craniospinal irradiation, but some of it happened before enrollment and RT was waived for pts with prior intracranial treatment. The protocol therefore tests a sequence (neuraxis RT as a platform, then intrathecal HER2 blockade) without fixing the RT component. The abstract does not report dose, fractionation, or how many pts got proton CSI versus whole-brain fields, which is the exact parameter a reader would need to decide whether this result depends on treating the whole neuraxis. The randomised MSKCC phase II of proton CSI versus photon involved-field RT established that the extent of the RT field matters in solid-tumor LM; this trial cannot say whether proton CSI or whole-brain RT is the better partner for intrathecal therapy, and it cannot say what RT adds over intrathecal therapy alone.

The response data support a real local effect in the leptomeningeal compartment, with complete responses in a subset, but without stated response criteria the split between partial response and stable disease is hard to interpret. LM response assessment is notoriously inconsistent across cytology, MRI and clinical status, and a single-arm study cannot calibrate it.

The toxicity profile is the most transferable finding. Intrathecal trastuzumab and pertuzumab at the recommended phase II dose produced little grade 2 or higher toxicity, and a meaningful fraction of pts remain on therapy years later. That makes the regimen a reasonable candidate for a randomised comparison.

What would make the survival claim wrong is confounding by modern CNS-active systemic HER2 therapy. Agents such as tucatinib and trastuzumab deruxtecan have changed CNS outcomes in HER2+ breast cancer, and pts continuing them on study could carry much of the survival observed here. The question the field needs answered next is whether intrathecal HER2 blockade adds to RT plus contemporary systemic therapy, and that requires a control arm.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Nearly all pts (97%) had WBRT or proton CSI before IT therapy, but RT was waived after prior intracranial RT and dose/fractionation is unreported. This positions neuraxis RT as the platform for IT HER2 blockade without telling you which field to use.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: IT trastuzumab 80 mg + pertuzumab 80 mg added little G≥2 toxicity, and 40% remain on therapy. Systemic agents could continue alongside it, so the OS reflects IT plus ongoing systemic HER2 therapy, not a replacement for it.

open_questions: What does proton CSI add over WBRT before IT HER2 therapy?
Does IT benefit hold beyond concurrent CNS-active systemic HER2 therapy?
Randomised confirmation vs RT plus systemic therapy alone

sites.intro: Mature 7.7 y f/u of the PEACE-1 2x2 factorial in de novo mCSPC: abiraterone OS benefit holds, SOC+RT mOS 4.6 y, same as SOC.

studies.name: PEACE-1 long-term OS
studies.tldr: Median 7.7 y f/u: abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (0.65-0.87) in de novo mCSPC; triplet vs ADT+docetaxel HR 0.68, mOS 6.2 vs 4.4 y.
details: 🔍 2x2 factorial phase 3, N=1173 de novo mCSPC, randomized 1:1:1:1
🔍 Baseline volume: 57% high-volume, 43% low-volume
📐 Abiraterone OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.87), p=0.0001 at median 7.7 y f/u

details.text: 📊 Median OS by factorial arm (y, 95% CI)
📊 Triplet vs doublet in the 710 pts on ADT+docetaxel SOC
📊 Triplet vs doublet by metastatic volume (interaction p=0.56)

details: 📊 SOC+RT mOS 4.6 y, same as SOC; RT-attributable OS HR not reported in source
🔗 vs initial analysis: abiraterone OS HR 0.82 (0.69-0.98), p=0.030 at 4.4 y median f/u (Lancet 2022)
⚠️ Low-volume triplet HR CI crosses 1; interaction p=0.56 does not prove a uniform effect
⚠️ Sources disagree: abstract high-volume 8y OS 20% vs 38%; OncoDaily reports 7y 22.4% vs 40.9%, HR 0.67
⚠️ Subsequent-line therapy at progression not reported in source

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase 3 with 7.7 y median f/u confirms the abiraterone OS effect seen at 4.4 y; triplet read rests on a docetaxel-backbone subgroup, not a randomized docetaxel comparison.
verdict.audience: De novo mCSPC, high- or low-volume, on ADT ± docetaxel

studies.significance: The four-arm medians carry the RT read: SOC+RT 4.6 y matched SOC 4.6 y, while SOC+RT+abiraterone reached 6.4 y vs 5.7 y for SOC+abiraterone. RT-attributable HR and the low-volume RT subgroup are not reported in this abstract, so it settles the systemic backbone around prostate RT rather than the RT decision itself.
studies.monday_clinic: In de novo high-volume mCSPC on ADT plus docetaxel, this supports abiraterone as the third agent at long-term follow-up; the low-volume triplet estimate is less certain, and it does not extend to metachronous mCSPC.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **2x2 factorial phase 3**, randomized 1:1:1:1, testing abiraterone/prednisone and/or prostate RT added to SOC. **N=1173**; this is the long-term update at **median 7.7 y** follow-up.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **De novo mCSPC**, 57% high-volume and 43% low-volume. Overall analysis population n=1172 in the trade-press report.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: SOC was **ADT with or without docetaxel**; abiraterone acetate plus prednisone was the randomized add-on. 710 pts received ADT+docetaxel as SOC.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Prostate RT was one factorial randomization; dose, fractionation and target volume not reported in source. **SOC+RT mOS 4.6 y (4.0-5.2) vs SOC 4.6 y (4.1-5.5)**; RT-specific HR and volume-stratified RT data not in this abstract.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: With vs without abiraterone: **mOS 6.1 vs 4.6 y**, 8y OS **40.3% vs 29.5%** (trade-press figures). Arm-level and triplet numbers are in the detail tables.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The initial PEACE-1 analysis reported abiraterone OS **HR 0.82 (0.69-0.98)** at 4.4 y; the estimate is now **HR 0.75** with longer follow-up. ARASENS is the other randomized triplet dataset in mCSPC, using darolutamide rather than abiraterone.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents de novo mCSPC, high- or low-volume, on ADT with or without docetaxel. Does not represent metachronous mCSPC after prior local therapy or castration-resistant disease.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Low-volume triplet HR 0.74 has a CI to 1.05, and a nonsignificant interaction test is not evidence of equal benefit. The abstract and trade-press report give **different high-volume landmark rates and HRs**; subsequent therapy is not reported.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: A long-term OS effect that holds or strengthens past 7 years in a factorial trial supports abiraterone in the de novo mCSPC backbone. What it does not settle is whether low-volume pts need docetaxel at all once an ARSI is on board.

studies.interpretation:
The main value of this update is durability. Intensification trials in mCSPC usually report once, near their event threshold, and later follow-up is uncommon, which is the point the authors make themselves. Here the abiraterone hazard ratio moved from 0.82 at a median 4.4 years to 0.75 at a median 7.7 years, and its interval now sits well clear of 1. A benefit that holds or widens as the control arm matures argues against an early separation that later fades, and that is the property a clinician most needs before committing a man with de novo metastatic disease to years of added therapy.

The triplet result is where a careful reader should slow down. The 710 men on ADT plus docetaxel make up a large group, and in them abiraterone gave HR 0.68 with median OS 6.2 vs 4.4 years and 8-year OS 40.3% vs 27.1%. But docetaxel was part of the SOC backbone, not one of the randomized factors, so this is a within-stratum comparison. Abiraterone was randomized inside that group, so the abiraterone effect there is internally valid. What the trial cannot show is whether docetaxel adds anything once abiraterone is given. PEACE-1 and ARASENS together back a triplet built on docetaxel, and neither was designed to test dropping docetaxel from it.

The volume analysis needs the same discipline. The interaction p of 0.56 is often read as showing benefit regardless of volume, and the authors frame it that way. A nonsignificant interaction in a subgroup this size shows only that heterogeneity was not detected. The high-volume estimate (HR 0.68, interval 0.54 to 0.85) is solid. The low-volume estimate (HR 0.74, interval 0.52 to 1.05) points the same way but is not conclusive alone, and low-volume men are exactly the ones whose long natural history makes added toxicity matter most. The authors' line about almost twice as many long-term survivors applies to high-volume disease (20% vs 38% at 8 years in the abstract), not to everyone.

There is a reporting problem to keep in mind. The trade-press account gives 7-year high-volume OS of 22.4% vs 40.9% and HR 0.67, while the abstract gives 8-year rates of 20% vs 38% and HR 0.68. These are probably different landmarks or data cuts, not errors, but anyone quoting a high-volume survival figure should cite the slide set or the eventual paper, not either secondary source.

For the radiation reader, this abstract adds little directly. SOC+RT median OS equals SOC at 4.6 years, and the RT-attributable hazard ratio and the low-volume RT analysis, where the prostate RT question actually lives, are not reported here. Comparing medians across factorial arms (6.4 years with RT plus abiraterone vs 5.7 years with abiraterone alone) is tempting but unadjusted, and it should not be read as an RT effect. What the update does provide is confidence that the systemic backbone used alongside prostate RT in low-volume de novo disease keeps its survival benefit over the long term. Subsequent-line therapy is not reported, so how much of the control arm's survival reflects later ARSI exposure cannot be judged from these sources.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SOC+RT mOS 4.6 y matched SOC 4.6 y, and SOC+RT+abiraterone reached 6.4 y vs 5.7 y for SOC+abiraterone. No RT HR or low-volume RT subgroup in this abstract, so it confirms the systemic backbone used with prostate RT rather than informing the RT decision.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Triplet ADT+docetaxel+abiraterone gave mOS 6.2 vs 4.4 y and 8y OS 40.3% vs 27.1% over the doublet. High-volume HR 0.68 is firm; low-volume HR 0.74 has a CI reaching 1.05. Backs abiraterone as the add-on for docetaxel-treated de novo pts; whether docetaxel can be dropped is untested.

open_questions: Triplet benefit in low-volume de novo mCSPC

Can docetaxel be omitted when an ARSI is given

related_trials.brief_summary:
This study is being done to answer the following question: can the chance of prostate cancer growing or spreading be lowered by adding a drug to the usual combination of drugs?

This study would like to find out if this approach is better or worse than the usual approach for prostate cancer.

The usual approach for patients who are not in a study is hormone treatment with Androgen Deprivation Therapy (ADT) and Androgen-Receptor Pathway Inhibitor (ARPI).

papers.title: Long-term overall survival with abiraterone acetate plus prednisone in the PEACE-1 phase 3 trial for de novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2215O · Proffered paper: Genitourinary tumours, prostate, penile and testis · 2026-10-24 · presented by Karim Fizazi (Lille, France) · NCT01957436

Background: Recent trials demonstrated the benefit of systemic treatment intensification in mCSPC. However, long-term analyses are rare, especially for pharma industry trials. PEACE-1 (NCT01957436) is a 2x2 factorial phase 3 randomized trial that tested the addition of abiraterone acetate/prednisone (abiraterone) and/or prostate radiotherapy (RT) to standard of care (SOC) consisting of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with or without docetaxel.
Methods: 1173 men (57% high-, 43% low-volume) with de novo mCSPC were randomized (1:1:1:1) to SOC, SOC+abiraterone, SOC+RT or SOC+abiraterone+RT. The initial analysis (median follow-up: 4.4 years [y]) showed abiraterone improved overall survival (OS) (HR: 0·82, 95% CI 0·69–0·98; p=0·030) (Fizazi K, Lancet 2022). Here we report long-term follow-up results.
Results: The median follow-up is 7.7 y. Abiraterone significantly improved survival (HR: 0.75 [95%CI: 0.65-0.87], p=0.0001) with median OS of 4.6 y (4.1-5.5) for SOC, 4.6 y (4.0-5.2) for SOC+RT, 5.7 y (4.8-6.6) for SOC+abiraterone, and 6.4 y (5.5-7.6) for SOC+RT+abiraterone, respectively. In the subgroup of 710 patients who received ADT+docetaxel as their SOC, adding abiraterone also improved survival (HR: 0.68 [0.56-0.82]), with a median OS of 4.4 y (4.0-4.9) for ADT+docetaxel (doublet) and 6.2 y (5.2-7.3) for ADT+docetaxel+abiraterone (triplet), resulting in 8-year survival rates of 27.1% (22.1-32.9) and 40.3% (34.3-46.6), respectively. The favorable effect of triplet therapy on OS was independent of metastatic extent (interaction test p= 0.56): median OS was 3.5 y (3.2-4.0) vs 4.6y (3.9-6.1) in patients with high-volume (HR: 0.68 [0,54; 0,85]) and 6.2 y (5.4-8.1) vs 7.8 y (6.4-NR) in patients with low-volume (HR: 0.74 [0.52-1.05]), for doublet versus triplet respectively. In patients with high-volume, 8-year OS rates were 20% (14.6-26.7) with doublet vs 38% (31.3-45.1) with triplet therapy.
Conclusions: Very long-term follow-up shows a major OS benefit of adding abiraterone to SOC for patients with mCSPC, irrespective of metastatic extent. Triplet therapy with ADT+docetaxel+abiraterone is associated with almost twice as many long-term survivors in some subgroups.
Clinical trial identification: NCT01957436.

papers.title: Radiation therapy followed by intrathecal (IT) trastuzumab/pertuzumab in the management of HER2+ breast leptomeningeal metastasis: Results from a phase II multi-institutional study, (INSPIRE-LM)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1768RO · Rapid oral 2: Breast cancer, advanced stage · 2026-10-26 · presented by Kamran Ahmed (Tampa, United States of America) · NCT04588545

Background: Treatment options for HER2+ leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) remain limited. We previously reported 80 mg as the recommended phase II dose of IT pertuzumab alongside 80 mg IT trastuzumab and now report preliminary results from the phase II study.
Methods: The study is a multi-institutional, phase II trial of radiation therapy (RT) followed by IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab in the management of HER2+ breast LM. HER2+ LM patients with a life expectancy > 8 weeks, and KPS ≥ 60 were eligible. RT was completed prior to the delivery of IT therapy but was not required in patients that received prior intracranial RT. Patients could continue treatment with systemic agents if controlling disease and LM developed while on these therapies. The primary objective was to evaluate overall survival (OS) following study treatment. Secondary objectives included LM progression free survival (LM-PFS) and LM response.
Results: A total of 30 patients were enrolled between November 2022 and May 2026. Median age was 48 (range: 33-65) and 15 patients (50%) had a baseline KPS </= 70. The median number of prior systemic therapies was 34 (range: 1-9). Most patients received whole brain radiation therapy or proton cranial spinal irradiation (n=29; 97%) either prior to IT therapy or before study entry. Median follow-up is 26 months. The study met its predetermined endpoint for OS. Median survival is 36.2 months (95% CI: 19.4 – Not reached (NR)) with a 12-month OS of 79%. Median LM progression free survival (LM-PFS) is 19.3 months (95% CI 7.2 – NR) with a 12-month LM-PFS of 61%. The best LM response was a complete response in 5 (17%), partial response in 5 (17%), and stable disease in 17 (57%). The most common grade ≥ 2 adverse events attributed to IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab included nausea/vomiting (n=3; 10%), fatigue (n=2; 7%), and headache (n=2; 7%). Currently, twelve patients (40%) continue study therapy with 38.7 months as the longest treatment duration.
Conclusions: The study met its predetermined endpoint for OS with the longest median OS reported to date in HER2+ LM. Complete responses were noted in a subset of patients. IT trastuzumab/pertuzumab should be considered in the management of HER2+ LM.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04588545.

papers.title: BRIDGET: A phase II trial of tucatinib added to trastuzumab/pertuzumab or ado-trastuzumab emtansine after isolated intracranial progression in patients with advanced HER2-positive breast cancer
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1767RO · Rapid oral 2: Breast cancer, advanced stage · 2026-10-26 · presented by Sarah Sammons (Baltimore, United States of America) · NCT05323955

Background: Isolated CNS relapse/progression (ICP) is a frequent occurrence in patients (pts) with HER2+ MBC. Current guidelines recommend local therapy and continuation of same systemic regimen. The impact of adjusting the systemic regimen to include a CNS-active agent is unknown. Tucatinib demonstrated significant intracranial activity in HER2CLIMB when delivered with capecitabine/trastuzumab. BRIDGET is a prospective trial to add a brain-penetrant TKI post radiation to ongoing therapy in attempts to prolong intracranial disease control in pts with stable or no extracranial disease (ECD).
Methods: Single-arm phase II trial of pts with HER2+ MBC experiencing a first or second isolated intracranial event with stable/no ECD on HP or T-DM1 within 12 wks of stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). Key eligibility: ECOG PS 0–2; SRS to all brain lesions ≥5mm, no prior HER2/EGFR TKI. Whole-brain radiation was exclusionary. Tucatinib 300 mg BID was added continuously to ongoing HP or T-DM1 therapy. Primary endpoint: intracranial PFS (iPFS) per RANO-BM compared with a historical exponential control (median of 5.0 mos) using a one-sample log-rank test (one-sided α=0.05; 90% power; N=43 evaluable).
Results: Of 48 enrolled pts, 47 were evaluable (median age 53.5 yrs; 66% ER+). Most pts (66%) had no ECD at enrollment, were treated with backbone HP (93.6%) and enrolled after their first intracranial event (80.9%). At a median follow-up of 19.6 mos (95% CI 15.6–26.1), intracranial progression occurred in 17 pts (36.2%); median iPFS was not reached (one-sample log-rank p<0.0001 for H0: median iPFS=5 mos). The 6-, 12-, and 18-mo iPFS rates were 91%, 64%, and 59%, respectively. Extracranial progression was rare (2 pts, 4.3%). The safety profile was favorable: grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 15% (7/47).
Conclusions: The addition of tucatinib to HP after radiation met the study’s primary endpoint, with more than half of patients remaining free of intracranial progression at 18 months. These findings support the addition of early tucatinib after local therapy as a well-tolerated strategy to improve intracranial disease control in a HER2+ isolated brain progression population.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05323955.
